findings.label: F1
findings.problem: In TimelineBuilder.#addSelected, stops with no selected place are always listed after the free time and the drive to the next selected stop. When such a stop's set time falls inside that drive, the schedule lists it after a drive that ends later than the stop's own time. So scheduleOf() does not return entries in time order. The comment on #waiting (lines 72-73) says this order 'keeps the entries in time order', and domain model 4.1 says scheduleOf() is 'in time order'. The unplaced stop also shows at a time when the party is still driving.
findings.failure_case: I ran timelineOf on these inputs. The day starts at 9:00. Stop A is selected and takes 60 minutes. Dinner has no place and is set for 10:10. Stop B is selected and takes 30 minutes. The drives are [0, 20, 20, 10]. The result is: drive 9:00–9:00, A 9:00–10:00, drive 10:00–10:20, dinner 10:10, B 10:20–10:50. Dinner at 10:10 comes after a drive that ends at 10:20. A user who sets dinner a few minutes after the previous stop ends will see this.
findings.label_reason: The app's output differs from what its own comment and docstring promise (time order), and a real user reaches this by giving an unplaced stop a set time a little after the previous stop ends. The change added this code. The implementer can decline it by pointing to the domain model's rule that an unplaced stop 'comes after the free time and drive'.

findings.label: F6
findings.problem: scheduleTimeAt() returns null for any minute at or past 2 × 1440, the day after the day's own next day. No test reaches this case. If the `minute >= 2 * MINUTES_IN_DAY` check were deleted, every test would still pass. A time on the third calendar day would then show as a wrong 'next day' time.
findings.failure_case: Delete `|| minute >= 2 * MINUTES_IN_DAY` from scheduleTimeAt. Then a schedule entry at minute 2900 shows as 00:20 on the next day instead of being empty, and no test in calendar-schedule.test.ts or anywhere else fails.
findings.label_reason: This is new behavior a caller can see (an empty time), and no test checks it. F1 to F5 don't fit because the code is right as written. The change added it.

dropped.problem: minutesOpen might miscount periods that wrap past Saturday night into Sunday, or count the same visit twice across the shifted weeks.
dropped.label: D1
dropped.reason: A period's close is moved into (open, open + one week], so the four shifted copies of a period never overlap each other, and an overlap can't be counted twice. The test 'reads hours that run from Saturday night into Sunday' runs the wrap case and gets the right totals: 60 minutes on Sunday, and 180 minutes on Saturday.

dropped.problem: #driveMinutesOf checks which stops are selected by selectedPlace, while the timeline checks visitTimeInMinutes. The two could disagree, so the segments wouldn't line up with the selected stops.
dropped.label: D1
dropped.reason: Stop.#refuseBrokenSelection and the visitTimeInMinutes setter refuse a visit time without a selected place. checkedVisitTime refuses a null visit time when a place is selected. So visitTimeInMinutes is non-null exactly when selectedPlace is non-null.

dropped.problem: The new weekday getter might map getUTCDay() to the wrong weekday name.
dropped.label: D1
dropped.reason: WEEKDAYS starts with 'sunday' at index 0, the same order as getUTCDay(). The date is built with Date.UTC, so the local time zone has no effect. The test 'reads the weekday from the day's date' checks it.
